name: Items ids or quick refs
description:
1. **Objective:** give models a stable, code-owned way to embed item refs (chat, message, board, column, profile, file, project) in their answers so the client can navigate — "quick refs" typed by the model were rejected as ambiguous.
2. **Format decided:** one scheme, `codx://<entity>/<id>[/<sub-entity>/<sub-id>][?project=]`, always rendered as a Markdown link with a server-sanitised label; full UUIDs in payload, short ids display-only.
3. **Implemented (foundation):** `codx/junior/refs.py` (grammar, builders, parser, `<item_refs>` context block) and `codx/junior/tools/item_ref_tools.py` (bulk/single tool, server-side labels, existence check).
4. **Registered:** `tools/__init__.py` now imports, exports and adds `item_ref` to `TOOLS` with `scope="global"`, `project_settings`, `session` and `dual_response`, so every model always has it.
5. **Pending:** refs in `project_manager_tools`/search outputs, per-turn block in `chat_engine.py`, injection in `smol_agent.py`, `GET /api/refs/resolve` router, and client-side render/click handling.

messages.content:
We must have an id ir quick ref for items like: chat, message, board, column,...   that we can use in the chat responses and can be easily identified by client like [Chat with custormer](chat://0970971) or Chat with custormer- response](chat://0970971/message/0970707) 

 we'll need to make sure all info reaches the models and probably create specific tools so models can create the item ref (so we keep the format in the code and not in the prompt)

Review and suggest how to implement and other better options.

### Acceptance criteria
Models can embed items refs in their responses that client can interpretate and use to connect with the elements

I'll review the codebase to ground the proposal in the actual structures (chat/message/board/column identifiers, tool registry, and how model output is rendered on the client).I reviewed the code that owns item identity, tool responses and message rendering before proposing anything. Below is the review, the recommended format, the alternatives, and the two foundation files (format + tool) I already created.

---

## 1. What the code actually gives us (facts, not assumptions)

| Item | Real identifier | Source | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Chat / task | `Chat.id` (UUID) | `db.py` | A task **is** a chat (`mode="task"`), so one `chat` entity covers both |
| Message | `Message.doc_id` (UUID) | `db.py` | Messages have **no** `id`, and live *inside* the chat JSON → a message is never addressable alone |
| Assistant reply | `response_message.doc_id` | `chat/chat_engine.py` + `chat_event_bridge.py` | Created **before** the AI call, so its id is known *while* the model writes → the model can link to its own answer |
| Board | **name** (folder) | `chat_manager.get_chat_file`, `tasks/<board>/<column>/` | `Kanban.doc_id` exists in the model but `kanban.json` is keyed by name |
| Column | **name** | same | `KanbanColumn.doc_id` exists but is unused/absent in the JSON |
| Project | `CODXJuniorSettings.project_id` | `settings.py` | Chats can be *owned* by another project (`Chat.owner_project_id`, `_resolve_owner_manager`) and `Chat.chat_links: List[ChatId]{chat_id, project_id}` already models cross-project links |
| Profile | `Profile.name` | `model/model.py` | |

Two current behaviours matter for the design:

1. **`ChatManager.find_by_id` matches `chat_id in path`** → an 8-char prefix already resolves today, and `project_manager_tools._short_id()` prints `chat.id[:8]` in tables. So a "quick ref" already exists informally — unstandardised, ambiguous on collision, and only unique *within one project*.
2. **Tool output never enters `Message.content`** (dual-response → `ToolEvent.output`, rendered collapsed). So a ref emitted only by a tool is *invisible* unless the model repeats it in its own text. Any tool that produces refs must return them in `llm_response` **and** say "insert verbatim".

---

## 2. Why the literal proposal (`chat://0970971`) will bite

1. **Prefix ids are ambiguous** — `find_by_id` returns the *first* path containing the substring. Two chats sharing a prefix → wrong navigation, silently.
2. **Messages cannot stand alone** — `chat://id` works, but a message ref must always carry its chat (storage is per-chat file).
3. **Board/column refs would need free text in a URL** — `My Board`, `Sprint/12` must be URL-encoded, otherwise the path splits wrongly.
4. **One scheme per entity doesn't scale** — `chat:`, `board:`, `profile:`, `file:` … and every new entity needs client config.
5. **Custom schemes can be stripped** — markdown-it keeps unknown schemes, but DOMPurify strips anything not matching `ALLOWED_URI_REGEXP`. A stripped href degrades to plain text (acceptable) or to a broken link (not acceptable) depending on the client config.

---

## 3. Recommended format

One scheme, entity as first path segment, sub-resources as nested segments:

```
codx://<entity>/<id>[/<sub-entity>/<sub-id>][?project=<project_id>]

codx://chat/<chat_id>                            chat or task
codx://chat/<chat_id>/message/<message_doc_id>   message inside a chat
codx://board/<board_name>                        kanban board
codx://board/<board_name>/column/<column_name>   board column
codx://profile/<profile_name>
codx://file/<project_relative_path>
codx://project/<project_id>
```

Decisions:

- **Full UUID, never a prefix**, in the payload. Short ids stay display-only (labels).
- **`?project=` only when the item is not in the current project** — same-project links stay short; cross-project ones are unambiguous (`owner_project_id`).
- **Always a Markdown link**: `[Chat with customer](codx://chat/…)`. Any renderer that ignores the scheme still shows the label; exports to MD/PDF/DOCX keep working; the model can even re-read its own refs as context.
- **Labels are built in code** (`sanitize_label`: no newlines, brackets → parens, truncate ~120 chars), so a tool can never emit invalid Markdown.

---

## 4. How the refs reach the model — and why not via the prompt

`SmolAgent.HARDCODED_SYSTEM_RULES` is the precedent to *not* repeat: a format in a prompt drifts and costs tokens on every request. Recommended combination (format lives 100% in code):

| Channel | What it gives | Where |
|---|---|---|
| **A. Every tool that returns items already includes `ref`** | The model just copies a string | `project_manager_tools` (`_task_dict`/`_task_summary`/`list_tasks`/`list_boards`), chat search, `create_task`, `profile_management` |
| **B. `<item_refs>` block injected per turn** | `current_chat`, `current_message` ("this answer"), `current_project`, boards/columns — available **without any tool call** | `chat/chat_engine.py` builds it → `SmolAgent` renders `refs.render_context_block()` into the system message (same pattern as the internal `profiles` header: consumed by the agent, never forwarded) |
| **C. `item_ref` tool** | Ad-hoc items the model learned elsewhere (a chat found by search, a file, a profile); bulk mode builds several at once | new `tools/item_ref_tools.py` (created below) |
| **D. `Message.meta_data["refs"]`** | Derived server-side by parsing the final content (`refs.find_refs`) → chips / dead-link detection / analytics, no schema change | `chat_engine` post-processing |

The only prompt-level text left is one line inside the injected block: *"copy a `ref`/`markdown` value verbatim; never invent ids"* — an instruction, not a format.

---

## 5. Other options considered

| Option | Verdict |
|---|---|
| `chat://` per-entity schemes | Rejected: one scheme per entity, collides with registered desktop schemes, `chat://id/message/x` already implies nesting anyway |
| **`https://<base>/ref/chat/…` deep link** | Strong alternative: survives every sanitizer, works when pasted in Slack/Jira, clickable in exported PDFs. Best used as an **alias** emitted by the same helper (one flag `ITEM_REF_SCHEME`), not as a second format |
| Custom `<codx-ref>` HTML | Rejected: sanitizer allowlisting, breaks exports and non-app renderers |
| Bare `codx://…` text (no link) | Rejected as primary (unreadable, auto-link surprises); fine as an extra machine field |
| Structured only (`Message.refs[]`) | Rejected as primary: loses position in the sentence; kept as a derived complement |
| `item_ref` tool as the *only* mechanism | Rejected: one extra round trip per mention and the model must know the ids in advance — that's why channel A/B exist |
| Short display ids (`chat:0970971`) | Display only: not routable, ambiguous across projects, needs a lookup round trip |

---

## 6. Client/server contract

`GET /api/refs/resolve?ref=<url>` (same `codx_path` middleware as the rest of the API):

```json
{ "valid": true, "entity": "chat", "id": "5f…", "sub_entity": "message",
  "sub_id": "9a…", "project_id": "p1", "exists": true,
  "label": "Chat with customer", "short": "5f0e1a2b",
  "url": "codx://chat/5f…/message/9a…?project=p1" }
```

Click routing on the client: `chat` → open chat (switch project first when `project_id` ≠ current); `chat/message` → open + scroll to `doc_id` + highlight; `board` → kanban board; `board/column` → focus column; `profile`/`file` → respective views. `exists: false` → "item no longer exists" toast instead of a failed navigation. Resolution must apply the **same permission path as `GET /api/chats?id=`** — refs are navigation hints, never authority.

**Streaming caveat:** content is streamed in chunks, so `[label](codx://cha` is momentarily incomplete. Parse refs on completed text (or per finished line), and let the renderer tolerate a dangling `](`.

---

## 7. Risks worth writing down

1. **Board/column rename breaks name-based refs** (folder rename). Accept for now; add `doc_id` to `kanban.json` later if it hurts.
2. **Cross-project**: without `?project=`, a chat id from another project silently resolves to nothing (`find_by_id` scans only the current project tree).
3. **Dead links from the model** — only `item_ref` + tool-provided refs should be trusted; the resolve endpoint is the safety net.
4. **Permission leaks** — a ref to a chat the user cannot read must not be emitted (tools run inside the caller's project manager: OK) nor resolved.
5. **`Message.doc_id` vs `Chat.id` naming** — keep them apart; a `message` entity without `chat/<id>` is meaningless.
6. **Collapsed tool output** — a ref that only lands in `ToolEvent.output` disappears from the answer; always duplicate it in `llm_content` and in the model's text.

---

## 8. Files to change (phased)

**Phase 1 — created now (format + tool, no behaviour change):**
- `codx/junior/refs.py` — grammar, builders, parser, label sanitiser, per-turn context block.
- `codx/junior/tools/item_ref_tools.py` — `item_ref` tool (bulk + single, server-side label resolution, existence check for chats/messages).

**Phase 2 — register + make refs reachable (3 small patches, not applied yet):**
1. `codx/junior/tools/__init__.py`: `from .item_ref_tools import item_ref, ITEM_REF_TOOL_JSON`; add `"item_ref",` to `__all__`; add a `TOOLS` entry `{"tool_json": ITEM_REF_TOOL_JSON, "settings": ToolSettings(project_settings=True, session=True, dual_response=True, scope="global").dict(), "tags": ["navigation", "refs", "links", "chats", "tasks", "boards"], "tool_call": item_ref}`.
2. `codx/junior/tools/project_manager_tools.py`: add `ref`/`markdown` to `_task_dict()` and `_task_summary()`, a ref per board/column in `_action_list_boards()`, a link column in `_action_list_tasks()`, and refs in create/update responses.
3. `codx/junior/chat/chat_engine.py`: build `item_refs = refs.render_context_block(...)` from the chat + `response_message` + board catalogue and pass it in the AI config; after the turn, `response_message.meta_data["refs"] = [r.to_dict() for r in refs.find_refs(content)]`.
4. `codx/junior/ai/smol/smol_agent.py`: accept `config["item_refs"]` and append it to the system message (one block, next to the profile-tools injection — no header, no provider payload change).
5. NEW `codx/junior/api/refs.py` router: `GET /api/refs/resolve` (permission-checked) so the client never re-implements the grammar.

**Phase 3 — client (other repo):** renderer intercept + click dispatch + dead-link handling.

---

## 9. Acceptance tests

- `refs.parse_ref(refs.chat_ref("…"))` round-trips id/project; a board named `Sprint/12` survives quoting.
- `item_ref` on a nonexistent chat returns `exists: false` (no fabricated link).
- A turn where the model must reference "my previous answer" produces `codx://chat/<id>/message/<response doc_id>` **without** calling a tool.
- Resolve endpoint returns `valid: false` for a deleted chat and never leaks a foreign project's chat.

---

## 10. Created files

<file_change path="codx/junior/refs.py" language="python" change_type="new" encoding="text">
"""
Item refs (quick refs): the single source of truth for the links models and
clients use to point at codx-junior items.

Why a module instead of instructions in the system prompt
---------------------------------------------------------
The model must never *compose* an item reference: it copies one from a tool
result or from the per-turn ``<item_refs>`` block. Keeping the grammar in code
means the format can change without touching a prompt, and that every builder
and parser (tools, API, post-processing) agrees on the exact same string.

Format
------
    codx://<entity>/<id>[/<sub-entity>/<sub-id>][?project=<project_id>]

    codx://chat/<chat_id>                            a chat or a task
    codx://chat/<chat_id>/message/<message_doc_id>   a message inside a chat
    codx://board/<board_name>                        a kanban board
    codx://board/<board_name>/column/<column_name>   a board column
    codx://profile/<profile_name>                    a profile
    codx://file/<project_relative_path>              a project file
    codx://project/<project_id>                      a project

``project`` is optional: when omitted the ref belongs to the project the client
is currently showing, so same-project links stay short. It is emitted when the
item lives somewhere else — chats can be owned by another project
(``Chat.owner_project_id``) and ``Chat.chat_links`` already models that.

Identifiers
-----------
    - chats/tasks: ``Chat.id`` (UUID). A task IS a chat, so there is no
      ``task`` entity.
    - messages: ``Message.doc_id`` (messages have no ``id``), always nested
      under their chat because messages are stored inside the chat file.
    - boards/columns: their **name** (``.codx/tasks/<board>/<column>/``),
      URL encoded. ``KanbanColumn.doc_id`` exists in the model but
      ``kanban.json`` is keyed by name, so names are today's only stable key.
    - profiles: profile name. files: project-relative path.

Rendering
---------
Refs are always rendered as Markdown links (``[label](codx://...)``) so any
renderer that does not understand the scheme still shows the label instead of a
raw URL. :func:`link` builds them with a sanitised label (no newlines, no
brackets, truncated) so a tool can never emit invalid Markdown.

Reverse direction
-----------------
:func:`parse_ref` / :func:`find_refs` are the only correct way to read a ref
back: client-side routing, ``GET /api/refs/resolve``, dead-link detection and
``Message.meta_data["refs"]`` extraction. A ref is a NAVIGATION HINT, never an
authorisation: the resolver must re-check existence and permissions.

Made with ❤️ by codx-junior
"""
import logging
import re

from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any, Dict, Iterable, List, Optional
from urllib.parse import parse_qs, quote, unquote, urlsplit

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# ── Scheme ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Single scheme with the entity as the first path segment: adding an entity
# (or a sub-resource) never requires a new scheme nor a new client setting.
SCHEME: str = "codx"
URI_PREFIX: str = f"{SCHEME}://"

# ── Entities ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

ENTITY_CHAT: str = "chat"
ENTITY_MESSAGE: str = "message"
ENTITY_BOARD: str = "board"
ENTITY_COLUMN: str = "column"
ENTITY_PROFILE: str = "profile"
ENTITY_FILE: str = "file"
ENTITY_PROJECT: str = "project"

# Entities addressable as the FIRST path segment. ``message`` and ``column`` are
# NOT here on purpose: they only exist as sub-resources of a chat/board.
ENTITIES = (
    ENTITY_CHAT,
    ENTITY_BOARD,
    ENTITY_PROFILE,
    ENTITY_FILE,
    ENTITY_PROJECT,
)

# Allowed ``<entity>/<id>/<sub-entity>/<sub-id>`` combinations.
ALLOWED_SUB_ENTITIES: Dict[str, tuple] = {
    ENTITY_CHAT: (ENTITY_MESSAGE,),
    ENTITY_BOARD: (ENTITY_COLUMN,),
}

# Query parameter carrying the project the item belongs to.
PROJECT_PARAM: str = "project"

# ── Limits ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Maximum characters of a link label. Long message excerpts would otherwise
# inflate the content and break the readability of the answer.
MAX_LABEL_CHARS: int = 120

# Characters of an id kept for display purposes ("quick ref" / short id).
SHORT_ID_CHARS: int = 8

# Matches a raw ref inside free text. Excludes whitespace and the characters
# that close a Markdown link so ``[t](codx://x)`` yields ``codx://x``.
_REF_PATTERN = re.compile(rf"{SCHEME}://[^\s<>()\[\]\"']+")

_WHITESPACE_PATTERN = re.compile(r"\s+")

# Trailing punctuation captured by _REF_PATTERN at the end of a sentence.
_TRAILING_PUNCTUATION = ".,;:!?"


# ── Value helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────


def short_id(value: Any, chars: int = SHORT_ID_CHARS) -> str:
    """
    Return the short (display only) form of an item id.

    Short ids are a convenience for tables and labels: they are ambiguous by
    design and MUST NOT be used inside a ref (``ChatManager.find_by_id``
    matches ``chat_id in path``, so two chats sharing a prefix resolve to the
    first one found).

    Args:
        value: Item object (``.id``/``.doc_id``) or id string.
        chars: Number of characters to keep.

    Returns:
        The leading ``chars`` characters of the id, or an empty string.
    """
    identifier = _value_of(value, "id") or _value_of(value, "doc_id")
    return identifier[:chars] if identifier else ""


def _value_of(item: Any, attribute: str = "id") -> str:
    """
    Return the string value of *item* (either the attribute or *item* itself).

    Args:
        item: Model instance (Chat, Message, ...) or plain string.
        attribute: Attribute to read from a model instance.

    Returns:
        Stripped string value, or an empty string when unavailable.
    """
    if item is None:
        return ""
    if isinstance(item, str):
        return item.strip()
    return str(getattr(item, attribute, "") or "").strip()


def _project_hint(item_project_id: Optional[str], current_project_id: Optional[str]) -> Optional[str]:
    """
    Return the project to add to a ref, or ``None`` when the current one works.

    Same-project refs stay short (no ``?project=``); a ref to an item owned by
    another project is qualified so the client can switch context before
    navigating.

    Args:
        item_project_id: Project that owns the item.
        current_project_id: Project the client is currently showing.

    Returns:
        The item project id when it differs from the current one, else None.
    """
    item_project = (item_project_id or "").strip()
    current_project = (current_project_id or "").strip()
    if not item_project or item_project == current_project:
        return None
    return item_project


def _encode(segment: Any) -> str:
    """Percent-encode a single path segment (``/`` and spaces included)."""
    return quote(str(segment if segment is not None else "").strip(), safe="")


# ── Builders ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────


def _build_ref(
    entity: str,
    item_id: Any,
    sub_entity: Optional[str] = None,
    sub_id: Any = None,
    project_id: Optional[str] = None,
) -> str:
    """
    Assemble a ref from already-resolved parts.

    Args:
        entity: Entity name (``chat``, ``board``, ...).
        item_id: Primary identifier (chat id, board name, ...).
        sub_entity: Optional sub-resource entity (``message``, ``column``).
        sub_id: Sub-resource identifier (message doc_id, column name).
        project_id: Optional owning project.

    Returns:
        The ``codx://`` ref.

    Raises:
        ValueError: When the entity or the identifier is missing/invalid.
    """
    entity = (entity or "").strip().lower()
    identifier = str(item_id or "").strip()
    if not entity or not identifier:
        raise ValueError("A ref needs an entity and an id")
    if entity not in ENTITIES:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Unknown ref entity '{entity}' (valid entities: {', '.join(ENTITIES)})"
        )

    segments: List[Any] = [entity, identifier]

    sub_entity = (sub_entity or "").strip().lower()
    if sub_entity:
        if sub_entity not in ALLOWED_SUB_ENTITIES.get(entity, ()):
            raise ValueError(
                f"Entity '{entity}' does not accept sub-entity '{sub_entity}'"
                f" (valid: {', '.join(ALLOWED_SUB_ENTITIES.get(entity, ()))})"
            )
        sub_identifier = str(sub_id or "").strip()
        if not sub_identifier:
            raise ValueError(f"Sub-entity '{sub_entity}' needs an id")
        segments.extend([sub_entity, sub_identifier])

    ref = f"{URI_PREFIX}{'/'.join(_encode(segment) for segment in segments)}"
    if project_id and str(project_id).strip():
        ref = f"{ref}?{PROJECT_PARAM}={_encode(project_id)}"
    return ref


def chat_ref(chat: Any, project_id: Optional[str] = None) -> str:
    """
    Build the ref of a chat (or task, which is a chat).

    Args:
        chat: Chat object or chat id.
        project_id: Optional owning project id.

    Returns:
        ``codx://chat/<chat_id>`` (plus ``?project=`` when given).

    Example:
        >>> chat_ref("5f0e1a2b-...")
        'codx://chat/5f0e1a2b-...'
    """
    return _build_ref(ENTITY_CHAT, _value_of(chat, "id"), project_id=project_id)


def message_ref(chat: Any, message: Any, project_id: Optional[str] = None) -> str:
    """
    Build the ref of a message inside its chat.

    The chat is mandatory: messages are stored inside the chat file, so there is
    no way to resolve a message without knowing its chat.

    Args:
        chat: Chat object or chat id.
        message: Message object or ``doc_id``.
        project_id: Optional owning project id.

    Returns:
        ``codx://chat/<chat_id>/message/<message_doc_id>``.

    Raises:
        ValueError: When the chat id or the message ``doc_id`` is missing.
    """
    return _build_ref(
        ENTITY_CHAT,
        _value_of(chat, "id"),
        sub_entity=ENTITY_MESSAGE,
        sub_id=_value_of(message, "doc_id"),
        project_id=project_id,
    )


def board_ref(board: Any, project_id: Optional[str] = None) -> str:
    """
    Build the ref of a kanban board (boards are identified by name).

    Args:
        board: Board name (or a board dict/object with ``name``/``title``).
        project_id: Optional owning project id.

    Returns:
        ``codx://board/<board_name>``.
    """
    name = _value_of(board, "name") or _value_of(board, "title")
    return _build_ref(ENTITY_BOARD, name, project_id=project_id)


def column_ref(board: Any, column: Any, project_id: Optional[str] = None) -> str:
    """
    Build the ref of a column inside its board.

    Args:
        board: Board name (or board dict/object).
        column: Column name (or column dict with ``title``/``name``).
        project_id: Optional owning project id.

    Returns:
        ``codx://board/<board_name>/column/<column_name>``.

    Raises:
        ValueError: When the column name is missing.
    """
    column_name = _value_of(column, "title") or _value_of(column, "name")
    return _build_ref(
        ENTITY_BOARD,
        _value_of(board, "name") or _value_of(board, "title"),
        sub_entity=ENTITY_COLUMN,
        sub_id=column_name,
        project_id=project_id,
    )


def profile_ref(profile: Any, project_id: Optional[str] = None) -> str:
    """Build the ref of a profile (identified by name)."""
    return _build_ref(
        ENTITY_PROFILE,
        _value_of(profile, "name") or _value_of(profile, "id"),
        project_id=project_id,
    )


def file_ref(path: Any, project_id: Optional[str] = None) -> str:
    """
    Build the ref of a project file (identified by its project-relative path).

    Leading slashes are stripped so the same file always renders the same ref.
    """
    value = str(path or "").strip()
    return _build_ref(ENTITY_FILE, value.lstrip("/"), project_id=project_id)


def project_ref(project_id: Any) -> str:
    """Build the ref of a project (identified by its project id)."""
    return _build_ref(ENTITY_PROJECT, project_id)


def ref_for(
    entity: str,
    item_id: Any,
    chat_id: Optional[str] = None,
    board: Optional[str] = None,
    project_id: Optional[str] = None,
) -> str:
    """
    Build a ref from an entity name and its identifier.

    Generic entry point used by the ``item_ref`` tool so the tool never has to
    know how each ref is assembled.

    Args:
        entity: One of ``chat``, ``message``, ``board``, ``column``,
            ``profile``, ``file`` or ``project``.
        item_id: Primary id (chat id, message doc_id, board/profile name, path).
        chat_id: Parent chat id (required for ``message``).
        board: Parent board name (required for ``column``).
        project_id: Optional owning project id.

    Returns:
        The ref string.

    Raises:
        ValueError: When the entity is unknown or a required parent is missing.
    """
    entity = (entity or "").strip().lower()

    if entity == ENTITY_CHAT:
        return chat_ref(item_id, project_id=project_id)
    if entity == ENTITY_MESSAGE:
        if not chat_id:
            raise ValueError("A message ref requires the parent chat_id")
        return _build_ref(
            ENTITY_CHAT,
            chat_id,
            sub_entity=ENTITY_MESSAGE,
            sub_id=item_id,
            project_id=project_id,
        )
    if entity == ENTITY_BOARD:
        return board_ref(item_id, project_id=project_id)
    if entity == ENTITY_COLUMN:

def sanitize_label(
    text: Any,
    max_chars: int = MAX_LABEL_CHARS,
    fallback: str = "item",
) -> str:
    """
    Make any text safe to use as the label of a Markdown link.

    Newlines are collapsed, backticks removed and square brackets replaced by
    parentheses: ``[`` / ``]`` inside a link label would terminate the label and
    produce broken Markdown.

    Args:
        text: Raw label (may contain Markdown, newlines, brackets...).
        max_chars: Maximum length of the label.
        fallback: Label used when *text* is empty.

    Returns:
        A single-line label, truncated with an ellipsis when too long.
    """
    value = _WHITESPACE_PATTERN.sub(" ", str(text or "")).strip()
    value = value.replace("`", "").replace("[", "(").replace("]", ")")
    if len(value) > max_chars:
        value = value[: max(1, max_chars - 1)].rstrip() + "…"
    return value or fallback


def link(label: Any, ref: str, max_chars: int = MAX_LABEL_CHARS) -> str:
    """
    Render a ref as a Markdown link with a sanitised label.

    Args:
        label: Human label (chat name, message excerpt, ...).
        ref: The ``codx://`` ref (see :func:`chat_ref` and friends).
        max_chars: Maximum label length.

    Returns:
        ``[label](ref)`` ready to be embedded in a message.
    """
    return f"[{sanitize_label(label, max_chars=max_chars)}]({ref})"


def chat_label(chat: Any) -> str:
    """Return the display label of a chat (its name, else its short id)."""
    name = _value_of(chat, "name")
    if name:
        return name
    identifier = _value_of(chat, "id")
    return f"Chat {identifier[:SHORT_ID_CHARS]}" if identifier else "Chat"


def message_label(message: Any, max_chars: int = 80) -> str:
    """
    Return a display label for a message: its first meaningful line.

    Args:
        message: Message object (may be None).
        max_chars: Maximum length of the label.

    Returns:
        First line of the content (truncated), or ``"<role> message"``.
    """
    content = str(getattr(message, "content", "") or "").strip()
    for line in content.splitlines():
        cleaned = line.strip().lstrip("#>*- ").strip()
        if cleaned:
            return sanitize_label(cleaned, max_chars=max_chars, fallback="message")
    role = str(getattr(message, "role", "") or "").strip() or "message"
    return sanitize_label(f"{role} message", max_chars=max_chars, fallback="message")

def render_context_block(
    project_id: Optional[str] = None,
    project_name: Optional[str] = None,
    chat: Any = None,
    message: Any = None,
    boards: Optional[Iterable[Dict[str, Any]]] = None,
    max_boards: int = 8,
    max_columns: int = 6,
) -> str:
    """
    Render the ``<item_refs>`` block injected into the system message.

    This is what lets the model link to *itself* (the current chat and the
    response message being written) and to the current project/boards without
    calling any tool: the assistant response message exists before the AI call,
    so its ``doc_id`` is already known here.

    Only INSTRUCTIONS are in the block, never the format: every link is built by
    this module.

    Args:
        project_id: Current project id.
        project_name: Current project name (display only).
        chat: Chat being processed (``Chat`` object or None).
        message: Assistant response message being produced (or None).
        boards: Optional board catalogue (dicts with ``name`` and ``columns``),
            typically ``codx.junior.tools.project_manager_tools._boards_info``.
        max_boards: Maximum number of boards listed.
        max_columns: Maximum number of columns listed per board.

    Returns:
        The block, or an empty string when there is nothing to report.
    """
    current_project = (project_id or "").strip()
    lines: List[str] = []

    chat_id = _value_of(chat, "id")
    chat_project = _value_of(chat, "owner_project_id") or _value_of(chat, "project_id")

    if chat_id:
        lines.append(
            "- current_chat: "
            + link(
                chat_label(chat),
                chat_ref(chat_id, project_id=_project_hint(chat_project, current_project)),
            )
        )

    message_id = _value_of(message, "doc_id")
    if chat_id and message_id:
        lines.append(
            "- current_message (this answer): "
            + link(
                "this answer",
                message_ref(
                    chat_id,
                    message_id,
                    project_id=_project_hint(chat_project, current_project),
                ),
            )
        )

    for board in list(boards or [])[:max_boards]:
        name = _value_of(board, "name") or _value_of(board, "title")
        if not name:
            continue
        board_link = link(name, board_ref(name))
        columns = [
            link(column, column_ref(name, column))
            for column in (board.get("columns") or [])[:max_columns]
            if column
        ]
        lines.append(
            f"- board: {board_link}" + (f" (columns: {', '.join(columns)})" if columns else "")
        )

    if not lines:
        return ""

    header = [
        "<item_refs>",
        "Links to codx-junior items use the codx:// scheme, always as a Markdown link.",
        "Copy any ref/markdown value returned by a tool VERBATIM: never build or invent ids.",
    ]
    if project_name or current_project:
        header.append(
            f"current_project: {project_name or '-'} (id {current_project or '-'})"
        )
    return "\n".join(header + lines + ["</item_refs>"])

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ItemRef:
    """
    A parsed ``codx://`` ref.

    Attributes:
        entity: Entity name (``chat``, ``board``, ``profile``, ``file``,
            ``project``).
        id: Primary identifier (chat id, board/profile name, path, project id).
        sub_entity: Sub-resource entity (``message`` or ``column``), if any.
        sub_id: Sub-resource identifier (message ``doc_id`` or column name).
        project_id: Owning project declared by the ref, if any.
        raw: The original string.
    """

    entity: str
    id: str
    sub_entity: Optional[str] = None
    sub_id: Optional[str] = None
    project_id: Optional[str] = None
    raw: str = ""

    @property
    def is_message(self) -> bool:
        """True when the ref points at a message inside a chat."""
        return self.entity == ENTITY_CHAT and self.sub_entity == ENTITY_MESSAGE

    @property
    def is_column(self) -> bool:
        """True when the ref points at a column inside a board."""
        return self.entity == ENTITY_BOARD and self.sub_entity == ENTITY_COLUMN

    def to_dict(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Return a JSON-ready view (used by the API and ``meta_data["refs"]``)."""
        return {
            "entity": self.entity,
            "id": self.id,
            "sub_entity": self.sub_entity,
            "sub_id": self.sub_id,
            "project_id": self.project_id,
            "raw": self.raw,
            "resolved_id": self.sub_id or self.id,
        }


def parse_ref(ref: str) -> Optional[ItemRef]:
    """
    Parse a ``codx://`` ref into an :class:`ItemRef`.

    Segments are split BEFORE unquoting, so an encoded ``/`` inside a board
    name (``Sprint%2F12``) does not break the path.

    Args:
        ref: The ref string (may be a full Markdown link's destination).

    Returns:
        The parsed ref, or ``None`` when it is not a valid item ref.
    """
    raw = str(ref or "").strip()
    if not raw.lower().startswith(URI_PREFIX):
        return None

    parts = urlsplit(raw)
    if parts.scheme.lower() != SCHEME:
        return None

    entity = (parts.netloc or "").strip().lower()
    segments = [segment for segment in parts.path.split("/") if segment]

    # Tolerate ``codx:///<entity>/<id>`` (empty netloc).
    if not entity and segments:
        entity = segments.pop(0).lower()

    if entity not in ENTITIES or not segments:
        return None

    item_id = unquote(segments[0]).strip()
    if not item_id:
        return None

    sub_entity: Optional[str] = None
    sub_id: Optional[str] = None
    if len(segments) >= 3:
        sub_entity = unquote(segments[1]).strip().lower()
        sub_id = unquote(segments[2]).strip() or None
        if sub_entity not in ALLOWED_SUB_ENTITIES.get(entity, ()) or not sub_id:
            return None

    project_values = parse_qs(parts.query).get(PROJECT_PARAM) or []
    project_id = project_values[0].strip() or None if project_values else None

    return ItemRef(
        entity=entity,
        id=item_id,
        sub_entity=sub_entity,
        sub_id=sub_id,
        project_id=project_id,
        raw=raw,
    )


def find_refs(text: str) -> List[ItemRef]:
    """
    Extract every valid item ref found in *text*, deduplicated and in order.

    Used to derive ``Message.meta_data["refs"]`` from the assistant answer (no
    schema change) and to detect dead links.

    Args:
        text: Any text, typically an assistant message content.

    Returns:
        The parsed refs, unique by raw string.
    """
    found: Dict[str, ItemRef] = {}
    for match in _REF_PATTERN.finditer(str(text or "")):
        candidate = match.group(0).rstrip(_TRAILING_PUNCTUATION)
        if candidate in found:
            continue
        parsed = parse_ref(candidate)
        if parsed is not None:
            found[candidate] = parsed
    return list(found.values())

messages, kanban boards and columns, profiles, project files and projects —

Design notes
------------
    - **The format lives in code.** Every ref is produced by

      from the :class:`~codx.junior.chat_manager.ChatManager`; a missing item is
      reported (``exists: false``) so the model does not publish a dead link.
      Boards, columns, profiles and files are emitted as given: their existence
      is verified by ``GET /api/refs/resolve`` (the same path the client uses
      before navigating).
    - **Bulk friendly.** ``items`` builds several links in one call (a task
      list, a board column, ...) so linking does not cost a tool call per item.
    - **The answer must repeat the link.** Tool output is attached to the
      response message as a collapsible property (``ToolEvent.output``), never

    requests: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []

    for item in items or []:

                "id": item.get("id"),

"""
ChatEventBridge — attaches AgentRunContext events to the chat response message
and persists it on EVERY change (crash-safe).

During an AI turn the SmolAgent emits :class:`engine.agent_runtime.AgentEvent`
notifications (tool start/end/error, run lifecycle).

Events are ASSOCIATED with the assistant **response message** that the
ChatEngine created BEFORE calling the AI — they are never emitted as separate
chat messages:

    * ``response_message.tool_events``      → list of :class:`ToolEvent`
      (one entry per tool call, updated in place: running → done/error). Each
      event also carries the tool's user-facing ``output`` so tool output can be
      rendered collapsed/hidden instead of polluting ``Message.content``.
    * ``response_message.lifecycle_events`` → list of :class:`LifeCycleEvent`
      (one entry per agent run, updated in place)

Tool output
-----------
TOOL_END events carry the dual-response tool's user-facing ``output``
(``ToolResponse.user_response``). The bridge stores it on the matching
:class:`ToolEvent` (``ToolEvent.output``) instead of it being merged into the
chat content, so the client decides how to display it. Cached tool calls do not
re-emit output (the first execution already delivered it).

Crash-safety guarantee
----------------------
On every event change the response message is:

    1. **Persisted immediately** via the ChatManager granular merge-safe
       methods (``add_message`` on first change, ``update_message`` after).
       If the process dies mid-run, every event received so far — including
       tool errors, run errors and aggregated analytics — is already on disk.
    2. **Streamed** to clients in real time via the EventManager so the UI
       can render tool progress live.

ADDED — streamed-chunk crash-safety (:meth:`maybe_persist_stream`):
    Streaming callbacks may call :meth:`maybe_persist_stream` on every flush;
    the bridge persists the response message AT MOST once per
    ``STREAM_PERSIST_MIN_INTERVAL_SECONDS`` (monotonic clock). A hard kill
    therefore loses at most that many seconds of streamed partial text while
    keeping disk I/O bounded.

ADDED — auxiliary message crash-safety (:meth:`persist_message`):
    Any auxiliary message produced mid-run (e.g. hidden reasoning messages)
    can be persisted immediately and idempotently. Persisted ``doc_id``s are

    message is on the in-memory chat) so information is never silently lost.
